title: Introduction to Authentication
summary: Frames the authentication module: why sites need accounts, the roadmap of security levels from plain-text storage up to OAuth, and the 'secrets' app (a Whisper-style anonymous confessions site) built throughout.

concepts.heading: Why authenticate
points: User-generated data (posts, likes, messages, recipes) must be tied to an individual, so each person gets an account identified by credentials, acting like an ID card in the database.
Accounts keep private data private: only the owner, after logging in, can see their messages.
Accounts also gate access by status, e.g. a streaming service unlocks content once a payment flag is set on the user record.

concepts.heading: Why it is hard
points: Creating sign-up and login is easy; making it secure is the difficult part.

The module climbs through levels: (1) store email and password in the database, (2) encryption, (3) hashing, (4) salting, (5) cookies and sessions, (6) secrets in environment variables, (7) OAuth / social login such as Google.
After building everything by hand, third-party helpers such as Passport are introduced to simplify it. Learning the bottom-up version first means you understand what libraries do.
Skipping ahead to OAuth is possible but not recommended.

concepts.heading: The app being built
points: A secrets-sharing site: anonymous posts, not linked to an email or username on display.
Three entry points: a home page with Register and Login buttons, and a secrets page only reachable once authenticated.
Starter files with styling are supplied so the focus stays on auth logic rather than Bootstrap/CSS.

pitfalls: (Extra) Treat each 'level' as a deliberately insecure stage that is fixed by the next one; do not ship early levels.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (section 35 has no file).
gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'Authentication overview': blurb on authentication vs authorisation; 3-5 tasks such as listing which of three sample pages need login, ordering the security levels, and sketching the register/login/secrets flow. Interactive demo: click-through flow diagram where a guest is redirected from /secrets to /login while a logged-in user passes.
